About National Trust of Australia (Queensland)
National Trust of Australia (Queensland) (NTAQ) is a membership-based environmental charity connecting people with significant places, collections and stories across Queensland. NTAQ manages a diverse portfolio of wildlife and heritage destinations, including one of the Gold Coast's most iconic visitor attractions, Currumbin Wildlife Sanctuary. As one of Queensland’s earliest nature-based tourist destinations, the Sanctuary is a physical embodiment of everything the NTAQ represents: to protect, conserve and celebrate Queensland's environmental, built and cultural heritage for future generations.

In this hands-on role, you will lead the ongoing optimisation of NTAQ's business systems, working across departments to identify opportunities to simplify processes, improve reporting and reduce manual effort. A key focus of the role will be supporting the implementation and ongoing development of our data warehouse environment, ensuring leaders have access to meaningful insights that support informed decision-making.

Using business intelligence, analytics and workflow automation tools to develop reporting, enhance processes and improve organisational performance, you will develop dashboards, automate workflows and improve the way information moves across the organisation. You will also work closely with software vendors and technology partners to ensure NTAQ continues to maximise system capability, maturity and return on investment.

This role is ideal for someone who enjoys balancing strategic thinking with hands-on delivery, contributing to future technology direction while delivering practical solutions that create measurable business outcomes for our people and guests.  By connecting systems, improving data accessibility and driving automation, you will help create a more efficient and commercially sustainable organisation, enabling NTAQ to continue delivering on its mission of conserving Queensland's natural, built and cultural heritage.

You are naturally curious, analytical and solutions-focused. You enjoy understanding how organisations operate and finding opportunities to improve processes, reporting and outcomes through technology. You can confidently work across both strategic and operational activities, contributing to future systems planning while also delivering practical solutions that create measurable business value. jobs.job_title: Graduate Software Developer — AI-Assisted Development (.NET / Azure)
jobs.job_description:
Learn to build real software, with AI at your side, on a product 1,200+ businesses rely on

REI Cloud is the property management and trust accounting platform built by the team behind REI Master. Australian-owned, 20+ years in the market, and used every day by holiday letting operators, permanent rental agencies, management rights businesses and serviced apartment groups across the country.

We're rebuilding and extending that platform on a modern Azure stack — and we're looking for one sharp graduate to join the dev team from the ground floor.

The role

This is a genuine ground-floor opportunity on a small team. There is no graduate program, no rotation, no six months of shadowing. You'll be given real work in your first week, your code will go in front of real customers, and you'll see the results of what you build.

You'll work alongside developers who know this industry inside out, on things like:

  • Building and shipping features in our line-of-business application used daily by property managers

  • Working across the stack — C#/.NET services, React/Angular + TypeScript and Blazor front ends, Azure SQL

  • Building and running workloads on Microsoft Azure

  • Trust accounting, bookings, channel management and inspections — complex, high-stakes domain logic where getting it right matters

  • Using Claude Code and AI pair-programming as a core part of how you work, not as a novelty

What we're looking for

Essential

  • A recent graduate in computer science, software engineering, IT or similar — or completing your degree at the end of 2026

  • Demonstrable fluency with AI-assisted development. Claude Code, or comparable tooling. You should be able to show us what you've built with it and talk through how you drove it

  • Solid fundamentals in C# or a similar object-oriented language, plus SQL

  • Some exposure to modern front-end development (React, Angular, TypeScript or Blazor)

  • The judgement to know when the AI is wrong, and the discipline to check

Nice to have

  • Personal projects, a GitHub profile, internships, hackathons or freelance work — anything that shows you build things because you want to

  • Any exposure to Microsoft Azure

  • Interest in property, accounting or fintech

Who fits here

We're a small team in one room. That means no egos and no passengers. You'll do interesting work and you'll do unglamorous work, often in the same day. You'll ask questions when you're stuck, take feedback without taking it personally, and be someone people are glad to sit next to day in day out. If that sounds like you, you'll do well here.

The non-negotiables

  • On-site, every day. This is a 100% in-office role at our Helensvale office. We've made that choice deliberately — a small team learns fastest and builds best in the same room, and as a graduate you'll get far more out of sitting beside developers than you would on a video call. If you're looking for hybrid or remote, this isn't the role for you.

  • Full, unrestricted working rights. You must be an Australian citizen or permanent resident. We are not able to sponsor visas for this role.

  • Already living within commuting distance of Helensvale, or relocating at your own arrangement before you start.

  • Clear written and verbal communication in English, — you'll be talking directly with the team and, at times, with customers. Our existing team members are from a broad range of backgrounds, and many are multi lingual. Of course this is a bonus for us, but strong English skills is at the core of this role.

What you get

  • Real responsibility and real ownership from day one

  • Direct mentoring from developers with deep experience in the platform and the industry

  • Modern stack, modern tooling, and a company that actively wants you using AI to work faster

  • A stable, profitable, Australian-owned business with a 20-year customer base — the upside of a startup without the runway anxiety

  • Gold Coast lifestyle, 20 minutes from the beach, no city commute

How to apply

Apply through Seek with your CV and a short cover note. In the cover note, please answer this in a few short paragraphs:

Tell us about something you have built with the help of AI coding tools. What was it, what did you ask the AI to do, where did it get things wrong, and how did you work out that it was wrong?

Tell us how you already fit with the non-negotiable aspects of this role.

We read these. It's the main thing we'll use to shortlist, so put your effort there rather than into a generic letter. Include a link to your GitHub or a live project if you have one.

Shortlisted applicants will be invited in for a chat and a short practical exercise at our office.

Start date: Flexible/part-time for students graduating later this year, otherwise immediate start

We're hiring one person and we'll move quickly for the right candidate.
